name: get_campaign_attribution_reports
description: REQUIRED FIRST STEP: before your first call, invoke tool_guidance for "get_campaign_attribution_reports" and follow it. The dimension names, filter syntax, date-range semantics, grouping rules, and query patterns live in tool_guidance, not in this description; calling this tool without them produces wrong or failed queries. If you skip tool_guidance, submit your first call with hasReadToolInstructions=false (the default); the tool will return status=READ_TOOL_INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED with the full instructions in toolInstructions — read them, then retry with hasReadToolInstructions=true. Revenue ranking: dimensions=[CAMPAIGN], metrics=[REVENUE], sortByMetric=REVENUE. Attribution data tool: all metrics (revenue, deal amounts, deal counts, contact counts) are scoped to the closed-won deal attribution pipeline. Use for revenue, attributed deal, and attributed contact questions. CONTACT_COUNT = contacts whose interactions influenced closed-won deals; this is NOT a "new contacts generated" metric. For non-attribution contact queries (new contacts, influenced contacts, sessions), use read_campaign_data with GET_ANALYTICS. TOP/BEST PERFORMING ASSET: use dimension=ASSET_TITLE; set sortByMetric to the metric the question asks about (REVENUE when unspecified, DEAL_COUNT for "most deals", DEAL_AMOUNT for "highest deal value", CONTACT_COUNT for "most contacts", ATTRIBUTION_COUNT for "most interactions"). Attribution metrics share a common unit across all asset types. Do NOT rank by calling getCampaignAssetMetrics per type — those engagement metrics (views vs. open rate) are not cross-type comparable. Scope note: this data covers closed-won / attributed deals only. For deals at any stage (open, opportunity, qualifiedtobuy, and so on), use read_campaign_data with operation=GET_ASSET_METRICS and assetType=DEAL (returns name, stage, amount, close date for all associated deals) or search_crm_objects with a campaign association filter. For long-running queries, this returns a PROCESSING status with a taskId to poll for results.

taskId.description: Poll for results of a previously submitted query. Pass the taskId from a PROCESSING response.

mode.description: Report mode. Only AGGREGATION is currently supported.

dimensions.description: How to group data (AGGREGATION mode). Max 2 per query. Omit for ungrouped totals. Key mappings: 'channels' or 'content types' (emails, ads, landing pages) -> ASSET_TYPE; specific asset names -> ASSET_TITLE; 'influence types' or 'engagement types' -> INTERACTION_TYPE; traffic/referral source -> INTERACTION_SOURCE; deal names -> DEAL_NAME; deal IDs (for links) -> DEAL.

metrics.description: Required: What to measure. REVENUE for attributed revenue (use for any non-deal breakdown like channel/source/asset), DEAL_AMOUNT for per-deal or total deal value (always grouped by deal), DEAL_COUNT for unique deals, CONTACT_COUNT for unique contacts, ATTRIBUTION_COUNT for touchpoint volume.

attributionModel.description: Revenue attribution model for the REVENUE metric. Defaults to LINEAR. See instructions for valid values.

campaignCrmObjectIds.description: Campaign CRM object IDs to scope the query. Empty for cross-campaign analysis.

startDate.description: Start of date range filter (YYYY-MM-DD). Must pair with endDate or both omitted. Filters by deal close date for REVENUE/DEAL_AMOUNT, deal create date for DEAL_COUNT, touchpoint timestamp for CONTACT_COUNT/ATTRIBUTION_COUNT.

endDate.description: End of date range filter (YYYY-MM-DD). Must pair with startDate or both omitted.

dimension.description: Dimension to filter on (e.g. ASSET_TYPE, INTERACTION_POSITION). Uses the same names as dimensions.

operator.description: Filter operator: EQ, NEQ, IN, NOT_IN, GT, GTE, LT, LTE, HAS_PROPERTY, NOT_HAS_PROPERTY.

value.description: Single value for EQ, NEQ, GT, GTE, LT, LTE operators.

values.description: Multiple values for IN, NOT_IN operators.

filters.description: Server-side filters on any dimension property. See instructions for examples.

sortByMetric.description: Sort results by this metric (DESC by default). Use to rank rows without post-processing, e.g. REVENUE returns highest-revenue rows first.

sortOrder.description: Sort direction for sortByMetric. ASC or DESC. Defaults to DESC.

limit.description: Max result rows returned by the server. Defaults to 100, maximum 500. When responseFormat=CONCISE, zero-value rows are filtered client-side after the server applies this limit, so fewer rows than requested may be returned.

responseFormat.description: Controls response verbosity. CONCISE (default) omits zero-value metric entries and drops rows where all metrics are zero, reducing token usage by up to ~⅔. DETAILED returns all rows and fields including zero values.

hasReadToolInstructions.description: Set to true once you have read the instructions for get_campaign_attribution_reports — either via tool_guidance (preferred) or from a READ_TOOL_INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED response. IMPORTANT: after calling tool_guidance for this tool, your very next call to get_campaign_attribution_reports MUST include hasReadToolInstructions=true. Omitting it (default false) triggers an inline READ_TOOL_INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED response instead of executing the query; do not omit it once you have already read the instructions from tool_guidance. Not required when polling with taskId.

name: manage_campaign_objects
description:
REQUIRED FIRST STEP: before your first call, invoke tool_guidance for "manage_campaign_objects".
Creates or updates campaigns, assigns campaign owners, and manages asset associations.

<prerequisites>
Use CRM tools to retrieve the campaign's campaignCrmObjectId before using CAMPAIGN_UPDATE or CAMPAIGN_ASSET operations.
</prerequisites>

<mandatory_confirmation_process>
Always show proposed changes in a table and get explicit user approval before creating or updating campaigns or modifying asset associations. This step is CRITICAL.

  <confirmation_rules>
  - **First confirmation only**: Add this line after the approval prompt: "Want to skip confirmations for this chat? Just ask."
  - **After 1 confirmation**: Stop offering the skip option, but keep confirming
  - **If user opts out**: Skip confirmations for remainder of session
  </confirmation_rules>

  <confirmation_format>
  Proposed Changes:

  | operationType   | Field       | Value             |
  |-----------------|-------------|-------------------|
  | CAMPAIGN_CREATE | displayName | Q3 Brand Campaign |

  Approve? [✅ Yes / ❌ No]
  Want to skip confirmations for this chat? Just ask.
  </confirmation_format>
</mandatory_confirmation_process>

<operations>
The `operationType` field is required on every request:
- CAMPAIGN_CREATE: set `createRequest` with required `displayName`, optional `startDate`, `endDate`, `goal`, `audience`, `notes`, `customProperties`.
- CAMPAIGN_UPDATE: set `updateRequest` with required `campaignCrmObjectId`, optional `displayName`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `goal`, `audience`, `notes`, `customProperties`.
- CAMPAIGN_ASSET: set `assetRequest` with required `campaignCrmObjectId`, `assetOperations` (non-empty list of `{action, assetObjectType, crmObjectIds}`). Each entry has its own ADD|REMOVE action. Check `assetOperationFailures` in the response — if non-empty, those operations failed; succeeded ones are already applied. Call CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES_LIST first.
- CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES_LIST: no additional fields required.
</operations>

displayName.description: Required. The campaign display name (max 255 chars).

startDate.description: Campaign start date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

endDate.description: Campaign end date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

owner.description: Campaign CRM owner ID, not a HubSpot user ID. Look it up with CRM owner tools.

status.description: Campaign status (sets hs_campaign_status). One of: planned, in_progress, active, paused, completed.

customProperties.description: Custom campaign properties as a map of property name to value. To set the campaign status, use the status field instead of hs_campaign_status.

createRequest.description: Campaign creation data. Required when operationType is CAMPAIGN_CREATE.

campaignCrmObjectId.description: Required. CRM object ID of the campaign to update. If you only have the campaign name, look it up first via CRM search or read_campaign_data; do not guess it.

startDate.description: Campaign start date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

endDate.description: Campaign end date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

owner.description: Campaign CRM owner ID, not a HubSpot user ID. Look it up with CRM owner tools.

status.description: Campaign status (sets hs_campaign_status). One of: planned, in_progress, active, paused, completed.

updateRequest.description: Campaign update data. Required when operationType is CAMPAIGN_UPDATE.

action.description: Required. The action to perform for this asset type: ADD or REMOVE.

assetObjectType.description: Required. The asset object type name (e.g. LANDING_PAGE, BLOG_POST, SITE_PAGE, MARKETING_EMAIL).

crmObjectIds.description: Required. CRM object IDs of the assets to associate or dissociate.

assetOperations.description: Required. One or more asset type operations. Each entry specifies an action (ADD|REMOVE), assetObjectType, and crmObjectIds, allowing ADD and REMOVE to be mixed in a single call. Each (action, assetObjectType) pair must appear at most once — e.g. ADD+LANDING_PAGE and REMOVE+LANDING_PAGE can coexist, but two ADD+LANDING_PAGE entries cannot. Operations are applied sequentially — if one fails, prior operations are not rolled back. Call CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES_LIST to discover valid assetObjectType values.

name: manage_custom_properties
description:
Creates custom property schemas on CRM object types.

<mandatory_confirmation_process>
Always show proposed schemas in a summary table and get explicit user approval before creating.
This is CRITICAL.

Set confirmationStatus to CONFIRMED after the user approves, or CONFIRMATION_WAIVED_FOR_SESSION if the user has opted out of per-action confirmations for the remainder of the session.
</mandatory_confirmation_process>

<write_result_handling>
Write tools return per-item results keyed by object type FQN. Each result has a succeeded flag and either successDetails or failureDetails. Always check each result, reporting successes/failures clearly to the user.
If failures are remediable, fix and retry those failures.
For successes, share the settingsLink from each successDetails with the user.
</write_result_handling>

<confirmation_format>
== Properties ==
Deal
* Risk Level (Drop-down): <description>
  - High
  - Medium
  - Low
* Loss Condition (String): <description>

Approve? [Yes / No]
</confirmation_format>

<custom_property_write_rules>
Behavioral Rules:
  - `label` & `description` should be in the user's language (and if english, `label` uses Sentence case)
  - You should NEVER recommend any property that could contain sensitive information or PII.
  - `groupName` should use pattern '{objectType}_information' (e.g., 'deal_information', 'contact_information')
  - Never show or mention the `fieldType` to the user - just reference the overall `type`.

Valid Type/FieldType Pairings:
  - string → text
  - bool → booleancheckbox
  - enumeration → select/checkbox
  - date → date
  - datetime → date
  - number → number
  - currency_number → number
</custom_property_write_rules>

name: submit_feedback
description:
Collects and submits user feedback about the HubSpot connector to HubSpot. Only after the user explicitly confirms the exact feedback to send.

<scope>
EXCLUSIVELY for feedback about HubSpot connector tools (search_crm_objects, manage_crm_objects, get_properties, etc.). Do NOT use for:
- Non-HubSpot tools (Slack, Microsoft 365, Notion, iMessage, Intercom, etc.)
- General AI/LLM quality (wrong answers, hallucinations, formatting)
- HubSpot product/UI issues unrelated to the connector
If the issue is not about a HubSpot connector tool, do NOT initiate feedback - tell the user this channel is for HubSpot connector issues only.
</scope>

<when_to_invoke>
Agent-detected: user corrects HubSpot connector behavior, reports it returned wrong data/errors, or is dissatisfied with a HubSpot connector tool.
User-initiated: explicit requests ("I want to give feedback"), or intent to reach HubSpot ("HubSpot should know...", "Tell HubSpot...").
</when_to_invoke>

<flow>
1. Agent-detected only: finish your answer first, then after a divider (---) note the connector issue and OFFER feedback; if declined, continue and never ask again this session.
2. Ask the user to describe the issue in their own words; WAIT.
3. Preview "Here's what I'll send to HubSpot: [their exact words]. Should I go ahead?" and WAIT for confirmation.
4. Only call this tool once the user confirms.
</flow>

<critical_requirements>
- NEVER call without explicit user confirmation of the feedback to send.
- The feedback field MUST be the user's own words - never auto-generate or paraphrase.
- Claude/ChatGPT thumbs up/down send feedback to Anthropic/OpenAI, NOT HubSpot; only this tool sends to HubSpot.
- NEVER submit feedback about non-HubSpot tools or connectors.
</critical_requirements>

feedback.description:
User's verbatim feedback about the HubSpot connector. CRITICAL RULES:
- Use the user's EXACT words. NEVER paraphrase, summarize, or rewrite.
- If the user said it in their language, keep it in their language.
- If the user hasn't typed specific feedback yet, do NOT fill this in yourself — ask them first.
- Avoid PII — use anonymized references.

triggeringToolName.description:
Name of the HubSpot tool related to this feedback.
IMPORTANT: This tool ONLY collects feedback about HubSpot connector tools.
Do NOT submit feedback about non-HubSpot tools (e.g. Slack, Microsoft 365, Notion, iMessage, Intercom, Bash, etc.).

feedbackType.description:
Category of the feedback being submitted. Used to triage and analyze feedback trends.
- PROBLEM: Something is broken or not working as expected (errors, incorrect results, bugs).
- FEATURE_REQUEST: A request for new functionality or capability, including enhancements to existing features that would require new behavior to be built.
- GENERAL_FEEDBACK: Opinions, observations, or suggestions about an existing tool or workflow — e.g., usability impressions, praise, workflow friction, or improvement ideas that don't rise to the level of a bug report or feature request.
- OTHER: Use only when the feedback genuinely does not fit any of the above categories.

sourceInterface.description:
Where the feedback originated.
- MCP_UI: Submitted from the dedicated in-app feedback UI rendered by the MCP host (e.g. a feedback form/widget the user explicitly opened).
- NON_UI: Submitted from a regular chat conversation (no dedicated feedback UI).

name: manage_segment
description:
Create a segment, edit an existing one, or add/remove CRM records from one. Set operation.type to CreateStaticSegmentOperation to create a new hand-picked static segment, CreateDynamicSegmentOperation to create a new dynamic (filter-driven) segment whose membership updates automatically, UpdateSegmentOperation to edit an existing segment's name, description, or filter, AddMembersOperation to add records to an existing static segment, RemoveMembersOperation to remove specific records from one, or RemoveAllMembersOperation to empty one entirely (the segment is kept).

<mandatory_confirmation>
This tool writes to the portal. Before calling it, you MUST show the user a summary of the exact action and get explicit approval:
- CreateStaticSegmentOperation: the new segment name, the object type, and how many records   (if any) will pre-populate it.
- CreateDynamicSegmentOperation: the new segment name, the object type, and the filter that   defines membership.
- UpdateSegmentOperation: the target segment (list ID) and which fields change (new name,   description, and/or filter).
- AddMembersOperation / RemoveMembersOperation: the target segment (list ID), the object type,   and the number of records being added or removed.
- RemoveAllMembersOperation: the target segment (list ID), and that this empties EVERY record   (the segment is kept, not deleted). Say explicitly that all records will be removed.
End with an explicit approval prompt (e.g. "Proceed? [Yes / No]"). Leave confirmationStatus as UNCONFIRMED until the user approves; only after they confirm, call the tool with confirmationStatus set to CONFIRMED. Do NOT set CONFIRMED before the user approves, even if the user asks you to "just do it" or to skip confirmation. On the first confirmation in a chat you may also offer to stop asking for the rest of the session; if the user agrees, set confirmationStatus to CONFIRMATION_WAIVED_FOR_SESSION on subsequent calls.
</mandatory_confirmation>

filterExpression.description:
The filter that defines membership. A DYNAMIC ("active") segment continuously reevaluates this expression, so records join or leave the segment automatically as they start or stop matching it. Required and must be non-blank.

    SQL-like filter expression defining segment membership.

    Property conditions compare the object's own properties and combine with AND, OR and parentheses: =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, CONTAINS, NOT CONTAINS, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, IN (...), IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, BETWEEN x AND y. Relative dates use NOW() or TODAY() with whole-day offsets only — DAYS or WEEKS, never MONTHS/QUARTERS/YEARS (write NOW() - 90 DAYS, not NOW() - 3 MONTHS). Dates compare at day granularity, and a date property never compares = or != against a relative time (use a fixed date like '2026-08-13', or a rolling window). Example: "lifecyclestage = 'customer' AND annualrevenue > 500000".

    Keep the expression small. Before it is stored it is expanded into disjunctive normal form, so every OR multiplies: OR groups of widths w1, w2, ... produce w1 x w2 x ... branches, and every ANDed condition is copied into every branch. Branches x conditions per branch is the stored filter count, and it must stay under 250. Multiply the OR widths before writing: 8 ANDed conditions with two OR groups of 5 and 10 alternatives is 50 branches and 500 filters, already rejected. To fit, narrow or remove OR groups, drop redundant ANDed conditions, or split the audience across more than one segment.

    Property names are the object type's internal CRM property names on THIS portal — look them up via your CRM property/schema tools, never guess from display labels or other portals; a name missing from the schema fails validation. Enumeration (dropdown) values must be the internal stored value, never the display label — a wrong value is NOT rejected: the segment saves and silently matches no records, so source stored values from the property definition. There is no dotted cross-object path (company.industry = '...' is invalid); conditions on a related record go inside ASSOCIATION(...) braces.

    Engagement conditions (opened, clicked, visited, submitted, last engaged) often have two valid encodings: a filter form below, or an analytics property on the object itself (recency dates, counts). When no matching filter form or event exists — or the request spans ANY asset rather than a specific one — search the object's real properties for an equivalent before reporting the condition unsupported (the look-it-up rule still applies).

    Beyond property conditions, exactly these filter forms exist; names and named arguments (name = value, never positional) are exact — no other functions or aliases. Notation: [x] is optional; a | b means exactly one. times counts occurrences (>=, <= or =); occurred bounds when (>, >=, < or <= with a date or NOW() offset); each is optional and they MAY be combined — except where a form states an EXCEPTION.
    - IN_LIST(list = 4521): member of another segment/list (id from searchSegments). The same filter keyed differently for workflows and imports: IN_LIST(workflow = '112233', [state = 'ENROLLED'|'ACTIVE'|'COMPLETED'|'GOAL']) (state defaults to ENROLLED, ever enrolled) or IN_LIST(import = '555') — no list argument in those forms.
    - FORM_SUBMISSION(form = '<guid>', [times >= 2], [occurred > NOW() - 90 DAYS]): submitted a form.
    - PAGE_VIEW(url = '<exact url>' | url_contains = '<substring>', [times >= 2 | occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS]): visited a website page. EXCEPTION: at most ONE refinement — a count OR a window, never both. The product stores one page-view refinement (the lists UI disables the second field too), so "twice in the last 30 days" is not expressible: keep the refinement the request makes primary, or ask the user which to keep. Page visits are ALWAYS this form, never UNIFIED_EVENTS — an event-form page-visit segment cannot be edited in the list UI. Negate with NOT_PAGE_VIEW(...).
    - ASSOCIATION(object = '0-2', association = 1) { industry = 'SAAS' }: has an associated record matching the braces; object is the associated record's object type id, association the numeric association type id between the two types, and the braces hold conditions on the associated record's properties. An ASSOCIATION body is conjunctive; OR inside its braces is rejected.
    - UNIFIED_EVENTS(type = '4-123456', [times >= 2], [occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS]) { [conditions] }: performed an event. The braces hold conditions on the event's OWN properties — take their names from searchFilterInputs (kind EVENT_PROPERTY), never from the segment object's schema.
    - EMAIL_EVENT(email = '169452110', app = 113, level = 'EMAIL_API_CAMPAIGN_GROUP', event = 'OPEN', [url_contains = '<substring>'], [occurred > '2026-01-01']): engaged with one specific marketing email. event is one of OPEN, CLICK, DELIVERED, SENT, REPLIED, BOUNCE, UNSUBSCRIBED, SPAMREPORT, PRINT. email, app and level come together from ONE searchFilterInputs (kind EMAIL) row — never mix rows or invent them. url_contains is valid only with event = 'CLICK'. EXCEPTIONS: occurred takes a fixed date only (rolling NOW() windows are rejected), no times, and no NOT form. For recency across ANY email ("opened an email in the last 30 days"), use the contact's email-engagement properties (e.g. hs_email_last_open_date) instead.
    Negate any form except EMAIL_EVENT by prefixing NOT, e.g. NOT IN_LIST(list = 4521). All forms combine freely with property conditions.

    Sourcing ids — users do not know these ids; look them up, never invent one (a guessed id creates a segment that silently filters on the wrong thing): list ids from searchSegments; association type ids, event type ids, event property names, form guids, workflow ids, import ids and email triples from searchFilterInputs (kind ASSOCIATION, EVENT, EVENT_PROPERTY, FORM, WORKFLOW, IMPORT or EMAIL), whose results include ready-to-use filter fragments.

    Property names are the object type's internal CRM property names on THIS portal — look them up via your CRM property/schema tools, never guess from display labels or other portals; a name missing from the schema fails validation. Enumeration (dropdown) values must be the internal stored value, never the display label — a wrong value is NOT rejected: the segment saves and silently matches no records, so source stored values from the property definition. There is no dotted cross-object path (company.industry = '...' is invalid); conditions on a related record go inside ASSOCIATION(...) braces.

    Engagement conditions (opened, clicked, visited, submitted, last engaged) often have two valid encodings: a filter form below, or an analytics property on the object itself (recency dates, counts). When no matching filter form or event exists — or the request spans ANY asset rather than a specific one — search the object's real properties for an equivalent before reporting the condition unsupported (the look-it-up rule still applies).

    Beyond property conditions, exactly these filter forms exist; names and named arguments (name = value, never positional) are exact — no other functions or aliases. Notation: [x] is optional; a | b means exactly one. times counts occurrences (>=, <= or =); occurred bounds when (>, >=, < or <= with a date or NOW() offset); each is optional and they MAY be combined — except where a form states an EXCEPTION.
    - IN_LIST(list = 4521): member of another segment/list (id from searchSegments). The same filter keyed differently for workflows and imports: IN_LIST(workflow = '112233', [state = 'ENROLLED'|'ACTIVE'|'COMPLETED'|'GOAL']) (state defaults to ENROLLED, ever enrolled) or IN_LIST(import = '555') — no list argument in those forms.
    - FORM_SUBMISSION(form = '<guid>', [times >= 2], [occurred > NOW() - 90 DAYS]): submitted a form.
    - PAGE_VIEW(url = '<exact url>' | url_contains = '<substring>', [times >= 2 | occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS]): visited a website page. EXCEPTION: at most ONE refinement — a count OR a window, never both. The product stores one page-view refinement (the lists UI disables the second field too), so "twice in the last 30 days" is not expressible: keep the refinement the request makes primary, or ask the user which to keep. Page visits are ALWAYS this form, never UNIFIED_EVENTS — an event-form page-visit segment cannot be edited in the list UI. Negate with NOT_PAGE_VIEW(...).
    - ASSOCIATION(object = '0-2', association = 1) { industry = 'SAAS' }: has an associated record matching the braces; object is the associated record's object type id, association the numeric association type id between the two types, and the braces hold conditions on the associated record's properties. An ASSOCIATION body is conjunctive; OR inside its braces is rejected.
    - UNIFIED_EVENTS(type = '4-123456', [times >= 2], [occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS]) { [conditions] }: performed an event. The braces hold conditions on the event's OWN properties — take their names from searchFilterInputs (kind EVENT_PROPERTY), never from the segment object's schema.
    - EMAIL_EVENT(email = '169452110', app = 113, level = 'EMAIL_API_CAMPAIGN_GROUP', event = 'OPEN', [url_contains = '<substring>'], [occurred > '2026-01-01']): engaged with one specific marketing email. event is one of OPEN, CLICK, DELIVERED, SENT, REPLIED, BOUNCE, UNSUBSCRIBED, SPAMREPORT, PRINT. email, app and level come together from ONE searchFilterInputs (kind EMAIL) row — never mix rows or invent them. url_contains is valid only with event = 'CLICK'. EXCEPTIONS: occurred takes a fixed date only (rolling NOW() windows are rejected), no times, and no NOT form. For recency across ANY email ("opened an email in the last 30 days"), use the contact's email-engagement properties (e.g. hs_email_last_open_date) instead.
    Negate any form except EMAIL_EVENT by prefixing NOT, e.g. NOT IN_LIST(list = 4521). All forms combine freely with property conditions.

    Sourcing ids — users do not know these ids; look them up, never invent one (a guessed id creates a segment that silently filters on the wrong thing): list ids from searchSegments; association type ids, event type ids, event property names, form guids, workflow ids, import ids and email triples from searchFilterInputs (kind ASSOCIATION, EVENT, EVENT_PROPERTY, FORM, WORKFLOW, IMPORT or EMAIL), whose results include ready-to-use filter fragments.

anyOf.description:
Edit an existing segment's name, description, or filter in place. This is a partial update: only
 the fields provided change; omitted fields keep their current values. It does NOT change
 membership directly (use AddMembersOperation / RemoveMembersOperation) and does NOT convert a
 hand-picked static list into a filter-driven one.

listId.description: The ID of the STATIC segment to remove every member from. This empties the segment's membership; it does not delete the segment, which remains and becomes empty (use DeleteSegmentOperation to remove the segment itself). Emptying runs as a background bulk operation, so the segment clears shortly rather than instantly. DYNAMIC (filter-driven) segments are rejected: their membership is computed from their filter and cannot be emptied manually — change the filter via UpdateSegmentOperation instead.

operation.description: The segment operation to perform. Set type to CreateStaticSegmentOperation, CreateDynamicSegmentOperation, UpdateSegmentOperation, AddMembersOperation, or RemoveMembersOperation.

confirmationStatus.description: User confirmation for this write. Defaults to UNCONFIRMED; the write is rejected unless set to CONFIRMED (or CONFIRMATION_WAIVED_FOR_SESSION) after the user approves.

name: manage_custom_pipelines
description:
Creates custom pipeline schemas on CRM object types.

Custom pipelines are available to paid tiers (Starter and above).

<default_pipeline_editing>
If portal does not have access to custom pipelines, can edit the default HubSpot-provided pipeline instead.
If the user confirms this is okay, set shouldEditDefaultPipelineInstead to true, and provide one schema.
</default_pipeline_editing>

<mandatory_confirmation_process>
Always show proposed schemas in a summary table and get explicit user approval before creating.
This is CRITICAL.

Set confirmationStatus to CONFIRMED after the user approves, or CONFIRMATION_WAIVED_FOR_SESSION if the user has opted out of per-action confirmations for the remainder of the session.
</mandatory_confirmation_process>

<write_result_handling>
Write tools return per-item results keyed by object type FQN. Each result has a succeeded flag and either successDetails or failureDetails. Always check each result, reporting successes/failures clearly to the user.
If failures are remediable, fix and retry those failures.
For successes, share the settingsLink from each successDetails with the user.
</write_result_handling>

<confirmation_format>
== Pipelines ==
Ticket
* Support Escalation: <description>
  - New (OPEN) -> In Progress (OPEN) -> Escalated (CLOSED) -> Resolved (CLOSED)

Deal
* Enterprise Sales: <description>
  - Prospecting (15%) -> Qualification (40%) -> Success (100% - Closed Won) -> Failure (0% - Closed Lost)

Approve? [Yes / No]
</confirmation_format>

<custom_pipeline_stage_metadata_rules>
DEAL (0-3):
  - `probability` (REQUIRED): decimal 0.0-1.0 (NOT percentage, NO % sign)
  - `state`: null

LEAD (0-136):
  - `probability`: null
  - `state` (REQUIRED): one of 'NEW', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'QUALIFIED', 'UNQUALIFIED'

NON-DEAL NON-LEAD:
  - `probability`: null
  - `state` (REQUIRED): 'OPEN' (active/in-progress) or 'CLOSED' (terminal/completed)
    - for TICKET (0-5), must be at least one 'OPEN' and one 'CLOSED' stage
</custom_pipeline_stage_metadata_rules>

objectTypeFqn.description: Fully-qualified name (FQN, e.g. TICKET) of the object type for which to create the custom pipelines

label.description: User facing name of the pipeline

displayOrder.description: 0-indexed order of the stage within the pipeline

probability.description: [For DEAL pipelines] Likelihood of the deal to be won and close successfully at this stage

state.description: [For non-DEAL pipelines] Whether the object is still OPEN or in a terminal CLOSED state at this stage. When for LEAD, represents whether the lead is NEW, IN_PROGRESS, QUALIFIED, or UNQUALIFIED.

stages.description: List of stages in this pipeline

displayOrder.description: Numerical order of the pipeline, default to 0 if unsure

reasonForRecommendation.description: Explains why this item was recommended to this portal, and/or how it should be used

customPipelineSchemas.description: Schemas of the custom pipelines (and their stages) to create for this object type

items.description:
MCP sibling of {@code CustomPipelineSchemasForObjectType} that keys the schemas by object-type
 FQN rather than {@code ObjectTypeId}, since MCP tools deal in FQNs. The FQN is resolved to an
 {@code ObjectTypeId} in the impl layer before delegating to {@code DataModelToolsManager}.

customPipelineRequestsForObjectTypes.description:
Set of requests to create custom pipelines, where each request specifies the schemas of the
pipelines (and their stages) to create and the FQN of the object type to create them for

confirmationStatus.description: Whether the user has approved this action. Must be CONFIRMED or CONFIRMATION_WAIVED_FOR_SESSION before invoking.

shouldEditDefaultPipelineInstead.description:
Only set to true when user explicitly confirms they want to edit their singular default pipeline for the object type
instead of creating a net-new custom pipeline, due to not having access to custom pipelines.

name: manage_landing_page
description: Create, edit, style, publish, clone, and inspect HubSpot landing pages. One action per call. Reads: MODULES, MODULE_TYPES, MODULE_DEF, MODULE_STYLES, MODULE_GUIDE, REVISIONS, TEMPLATES, FORMS, BRAND_KIT, LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES. Writes: CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE, CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE, UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE, CREATE_MODULE, UPDATE_MODULE, SET_MODULE_FIELDS, SET_MODULE_STYLES, SET_SECTION_STYLES, INSERT, REMOVE, REMOVE_SECTION, MOVE, SET_METADATA, PUBLISH, CLONE, RESTORE_REVISION. Read before write: MODULES before any edit; MODULE_TYPES before INSERT; MODULE_DEF before unfamiliar fields; MODULE_STYLES before SET_MODULE_STYLES. Writes mutate one shared draft — never concurrently. CREATE_MODULE authors a reusable custom module TYPE (not on any page — check LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES first, then INSERT the returned modulePath). BATCH IS THE DEFAULT for compound edits: group SET_MODULE_FIELDS/STYLES/SECTION_STYLES/METADATA/REMOVE/MOVE into one action=BATCH call (operationsJson, sequential server-side, returns batchResults). Max 10 operations per batch; at most one REMOVE/REMOVE_SECTION/MOVE per batch. NOT batchable (always separate): INSERT/CREATE_*/UPDATE_*/CLONE/PUBLISH/RESTORE_REVISION. If BATCH returns "not currently supported", fall back to sequential calls. CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE requires explicit user confirmation IN CHAT — choosing a template is NOT confirmation. Confirm before PUBLISH or RESTORE_REVISION. Never renders a card — after your LAST edit or PUBLISH, call the render tool. Examples: action=MODULES contentId=123 -> modulesJson. action=CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE pageName="Spring Promo" templatePath="..." -> {status,contentId,editorUrl}. action=SET_MODULE_FIELDS contentId=456 moduleId="hero_1" fieldOverridesJson={headline:"Hi"} -> verifiedFieldsJson. action=SET_SECTION_STYLES contentId=456 moduleId="hero_1" stylesJson={backgroundColor:{r:255,g:238,b:0,a:1}} -> verifiedStylesJson. Scopes: reads need landingpages-read or -write; writes need landingpages-write; PUBLISH additionally needs landingpages-publish.

action.description: Action to perform. One per call. READ actions (no side effects): "MODULES": list every module on the page draft. Each entry includes the module's field values, its layout position (sectionId, rowIndex, parentCellName when it lives inside a nested column, and cellWidth/cellX on the 12-column grid), and ownership flags (overrideable, globalOwned, globalPartialPath, themePartialOwned). Positions are populated even on a freshly created template page, before any edit. Capture a module's position here BEFORE you REMOVE or MOVE it so you can restore or reposition it precisely. Check ownership before REMOVE/MOVE: true global partials (header/footer) and global widgets are refused, but modules inside theme dnd_partial sections are removable and movable. "MODULE_TYPES": list available module types for this page's theme (call before INSERT). "MODULE_DEF": full field schema for a module type (requires modulePath). The response also includes the curated guide in moduleGuide when one exists, so a separate MODULE_GUIDE call is usually unnecessary. "MODULE_STYLES": read the layout styles (padding, margin, background, visibility) for a module (requires moduleId). "MODULE_GUIDE": (rarely needed — MODULE_DEF already returns the same guide inline) curated markdown for the modulePath covering required fields, common traps, and a minimal INSERT body. Errors if no guide exists; check MODULE_TYPES.hasGuide first. "REVISIONS": list recent page revisions for undo. "TEMPLATES": list landing page templates available in the portal (contentId not required). "FORMS": list forms available in the portal for embedding on THIS LANDING PAGE via the @hubspot/form module (contentId not required). This is the landing-page tool's own forms lookup and it is complete: an empty list means the portal has no forms. Never call manage_website_page (or a CRM tool) for form data while working on a landing page. Returns guid, name, portalId, formType, isPublished, createdAt, updatedAt. "BRAND_KIT": fetch the portal's primary brand kit (colors, fonts, logos) for THIS LANDING PAGE — complete on its own, and never to be re-fetched via manage_website_page — when brand-consistent content would help — e.g. picking a CTA color, a hero font, or a logo to drop into a header (contentId not required). "LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES": list the custom module types already in this portal's Design Manager, most recently updated first (contentId not required). Call this BEFORE CREATE_MODULE to check whether a suitable module already exists — reusing one is cheaper than creating a duplicate, and its modulePath goes straight into INSERT. Returns customModules (modulePath plus a compact field schema). Optional: limit (default 20, max 50). WRITE actions (mutate the same shared draft — issue them ONE AT A TIME, never in parallel): "CLONE": duplicate an existing page (requires contentId of the source page; optional pageName, slug and businessUnitId for the clone). Returns a new contentId. "CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE": create the page from a template (requires pageName and templatePath; optional slug and businessUnitId). MUST be preceded by a proposal card (call render_landing_page_ui directly with a "propose" target — there is no separate write step to propose) and an explicit user confirmation IN CHAT — never the first step of creating a page, and choosing a template is NOT confirmation. Returns contentId. "SET_MODULE_FIELDS": verbatim field patch on one module (requires contentId, moduleId, fieldOverridesJson). "SET_MODULE_STYLES": set layout styles (padding, margin, background, visibility) on one module (requires contentId, moduleId, stylesJson). Merge semantics — only supplied fields are updated. Call action=MODULE_STYLES first to see current values. "SET_SECTION_STYLES": set the background, padding, margin, or full-width of the ENTIRE SECTION band a module sits in (requires contentId, moduleId, stylesJson; moduleId is any module inside the band, used as an anchor). This is the correct way to do "make this section's background <color>" — do NOT inject CSS via SET_METADATA headHtml for section backgrounds. Merge semantics. Page-scoped bands — including theme dnd_partial sections — CAN be styled; only true global sections (header/footer/global widgets) are refused. "INSERT": add a new module (requires contentId, modulePath; then EITHER anchorModuleId+anchorPosition for anchor-based placement, OR sectionId+rowStart+columnStart+columnsSpanned for grid-coord placement; optional fieldOverridesJson). "REMOVE": delete one module (requires contentId, moduleId). If it was the last module in its section band, the now-empty band — background and padding included — is collapsed too, so no empty "Drop modules here" ghost band is left behind. "REMOVE_SECTION": delete the ENTIRE section band a module sits in — the whole top-level row, every module in it, AND the band's own background/padding styles (requires contentId, moduleId; moduleId is any module inside the target band, used as an anchor). Page-scoped sections — including theme dnd_partial sections like a logo bar — CAN be removed; only true global sections are refused. "MOVE": reposition module into its own new row (requires contentId, moduleId; then EITHER anchorModuleId+anchorPosition for anchor-based placement, OR sectionId+rowStart for grid placement). For MOVE, anchorPosition supports the new-row directions BEFORE / AFTER / START_OF_SECTION / END_OF_SECTION; in-row and stacked directions (IN_ROW_*, STACK_*) are INSERT-only — to place a module in-row or stacked, REMOVE it and INSERT with that anchorPosition. "SET_METADATA": update page metadata — pageName, htmlTitle, slug, metaDescription, featuredImageUrl, language, headHtml (requires contentId; all metadata fields optional). "PUBLISH": publish draft (requires contentId; confirm with the user first). "RESTORE_REVISION": roll back to revision (requires contentId, revisionId; confirm first). "CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE": create a fully custom landing page from HubL source you write. Use when no existing template fits the user's design — you author the complete HTML/HubL and pass it as hublSource. Requires slug and hublSource. Returns templatePath (always .html). No module editing is needed — the HubL IS the final design. hublSource must be under 1.5 MB. "UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE": replace the HubL source of a page previously created with CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE. Requires templatePath (from the create response) and hublSource; pass templateId too when you have it — it resolves the template even after a publish moves it. The live page reflects the change immediately — no separate publish step. Same hublSource size limit as CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE. "CREATE_MODULE": author a NEW custom module TYPE in Design Manager — a reusable module the theme does not have yet (requires moduleName, moduleHtml, moduleFieldsJson; contentId not required). Returns modulePath. This creates the TYPE only and puts nothing on any page: pass modulePath verbatim to action=INSERT to place an instance. Reach for it only when no built-in or existing custom module fits (check MODULE_TYPES and LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES first). Not tied to a page, so several CREATE_MODULE calls CAN run in parallel. "UPDATE_MODULE": replace the HubL and/or field schema of a module type previously created with CREATE_MODULE (requires modulePath from the create response, plus moduleHtml and/or moduleFieldsJson). moduleFieldsJson REPLACES the whole schema rather than patching it. Every page using the module re-renders with the new source immediately. Only module types created through CREATE_MODULE can be updated. "BATCH": run several operations in ONE call, executed sequentially server-side, stopping at the first failure (requires operationsJson). Batchable sub-actions: all READ actions, plus the write actions SET_MODULE_FIELDS, SET_MODULE_STYLES, SET_SECTION_STYLES, SET_METADATA, REMOVE, REMOVE_SECTION, MOVE — i.e. edits on modules/sections you ALREADY have IDs for. NOT batchable (their output feeds later work, or they change whole-page lifecycle): INSERT, CLONE, CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE, CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE, UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE, CREATE_MODULE, UPDATE_MODULE, PUBLISH, RESTORE_REVISION, BATCH. Returns batchResults with a per-operation outcome; committed operations are NOT rolled back when a later operation fails. Read MODULES first to capture the IDs each operation needs.

contentId.description: Content ID of the landing page. Required for most actions. NOT required for CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE (creates a new page), TEMPLATES, FORMS, BRAND_KIT, MODULE_DEF, and MODULE_GUIDE.

moduleId.description: Module ID to operate on. Required for SET_MODULE_FIELDS, SET_MODULE_STYLES, SET_SECTION_STYLES, REMOVE, REMOVE_SECTION, MOVE, and MODULE_STYLES. For REMOVE_SECTION and SET_SECTION_STYLES it is any module inside the target section band (an anchor). Find IDs via action=MODULES.

modulePath.description: Module type path (e.g. "@hubspot/rich_text"). Required for INSERT, MODULE_DEF, MODULE_GUIDE, and UPDATE_MODULE. Use paths exactly as returned by action=MODULE_TYPES, LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES, or CREATE_MODULE (a custom module's stored path can differ from the moduleName you sent, so never reconstruct it).

query.description: Substring filter. When action=MODULE_TYPES: filters by module type name. When action=TEMPLATES: filters by template name.

availableForNewContent.description: When action=TEMPLATES: filter to templates available for new page creation. Omit to return all templates.

folderName.description: When action=TEMPLATES: filter by folder name (e.g. "my-theme/templates").

themePath.description: When action=TEMPLATES: filter templates by theme path. Use for HubSpot themes ("@hubspot/elevate", "@hubspot/growth"), marketplace themes ("@marketplace/vendor/theme-name"), or custom themes ("my-custom-theme"). Omit to return templates across all themes.

responseFormat.description: Verbosity of the response. "DETAILED" returns all fields and is the default when omitted. "SUMMARY" trims verbose fields to save tokens on large pages: when action=MODULES, drops module field values and returns only module IDs, modulePaths, and section info. For MODULE_TYPES, MODULE_DEF, and REVISIONS, SUMMARY currently returns the same payload as DETAILED.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return for paginated read actions (MODULES, MODULE_TYPES, REVISIONS). Defaults to 50. Ignored for MODULE_DEF. For LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES it defaults to 20 and is capped at 50.

offset.description: Zero-based starting index for paginated read actions (MODULES, MODULE_TYPES, REVISIONS). Defaults to 0. Use the response's nextOffset to fetch the next page when hasMore is true. Ignored for MODULE_DEF.

pageName.description: Name for the landing page. Required for CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE. Optional for CLONE (defaults to a copy of the source page name). Also used by SET_METADATA to update the internal listing name shown in the HubSpot content listing UI (not the HTML title).

templatePath.description: Template path to build the page on. Required for CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE. Use action=TEMPLATES to discover available templates, then pass the templatePath exactly as returned.

templateId.description: Numeric template id, as returned by action=TEMPLATES ("id") and by CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE / UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE ("templateId"). Optional for UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE, where it is preferred over templatePath: publishing can move a custom template to a different path, and the id keeps working when it does. Ignored by every other action.

fieldOverridesJson.description: JSON object of verbatim field values (e.g. {"heading":"Close deals faster"}). Required for SET_MODULE_FIELDS. Optional for INSERT (sets initial field values on the new module).

stylesJson.description: JSON object of structured layout styles to merge. Required for SET_MODULE_STYLES (onto a module) and SET_SECTION_STYLES (onto a section band). Uses merge semantics: only supplied fields are updated, existing styles are preserved. Shape: {"breakpoint_styles":{"default":{"padding":{"top":{"value":20,"units":"px"}},"margin":{"top":{"value":10,"units":"px"}}}}}. Supported breakpoints: "default" (desktop), "mobile". Supported spacing sides — padding: top, right, bottom, left; margin: top, bottom. Each side is a Size: {"value":<number>,"units":"px"|"em"|"rem"|..."}. Background color (mainly for SET_SECTION_STYLES) goes in the top-level backgroundColor field as r/g/b/a: {"backgroundColor":{"r":255,"g":238,"b":0,"a":1}} (r/g/b 0–255, a 0–1). Section-only fields (SET_SECTION_STYLES): "forceFullWidthSection":true OR "maxWidthSectionCentering":<px> (mutually exclusive). Use camelCase keys (e.g. backgroundColor, breakpointStyles, forceFullWidthSection) — they mirror what action=MODULE_STYLES returns. Also supports per-breakpoint "hidden":true/false to toggle visibility. Layout only — for TEXT color use the separate textColor field, not this.

textColor.description: For action=SET_MODULE_STYLES: set the text color of ALL text in a module (headings, paragraphs, list items) to this CSS color, e.g. "#cc0000", "red", or "rgb(204,0,0)". This is the reliable way to recolor module text — it writes a scoped, !important rule the renderer applies to the module's own elements, overriding the theme. Do NOT hand-roll headHtml CSS for text color, and do NOT use it to recolor a whole section (use the section's sectionStyleVariant for that). Supply with moduleId; may be combined with stylesJson.

sectionId.description: Layout section ID to place the module in. Required for INSERT (grid-coord placement). Optional for MOVE (omit to keep current section). Find section IDs via action=MODULES.

rowStart.description: 1-based row position within the section. Required for INSERT (grid-coord placement). Optional for MOVE. Modules with the same rowStart and sectionId are placed side-by-side.

columnStart.description: 1-based column position on a 12-column grid. Required for INSERT (grid-coord placement). Optional for MOVE. columnStart=1 is leftmost.

columnsSpanned.description: Width in columns on the 12-column grid. Required for INSERT when using legacy grid-coord placement. Full width=12, two halves=6 each, three thirds=4 each. Omit when using anchor-based placement (anchorModuleId + anchorPosition) — width is computed automatically by stealing from siblings.

anchorModuleId.description: Anchor-based placement: moduleId of an existing module that an INSERT (or a moved module on MOVE) should land relative to. When provided, omit rowStart / columnStart / columnsSpanned — the backend resolves the target row from the anchor and (for INSERT) auto-redistributes column widths across siblings. Pair with anchorPosition.

anchorPosition.description: Anchor placement direction. Used with anchorModuleId on INSERT. Values: "BEFORE" (new module on a new row immediately above the anchor's row), "AFTER" (new row immediately below), "IN_ROW_WITH" (sibling cell appended to the right of all existing cells in the anchor's row — siblings give up width), "IN_ROW_BEFORE" (sibling cell positioned to the LEFT of the anchor within the same row), "IN_ROW_AFTER" (sibling cell positioned to the RIGHT of the anchor within the same row, regardless of any cells beyond the anchor), "START_OF_SECTION" (first row of anchor's section), "END_OF_SECTION" (last row of anchor's section), "STACK_ABOVE" (wrap the anchor in a column and place the new module ABOVE it as a stacked row), "STACK_BELOW" (same, stacked BELOW). STACK_* builds a "unified section" — both modules share ONE wrapper cell as separate rows (the shape the editor's drag-to-stack creates); use it instead of BEFORE/AFTER when the two modules should read as one visual group rather than independent section rows. STACK requires a module anchor inside a section (not a top-level section id).

htmlTitle.description: HTML <title> tag for the page (~50–60 chars). Only used for SET_METADATA. Omit to leave unchanged.

slug.description: URL slug (lowercase, hyphenated, no leading slash). Used for SET_METADATA (omit to leave unchanged), CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE (omit to derive from pageName), CLONE (omit to auto-generate), or CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE (required — used as the template name).

metaDescription.description: Meta description for search snippets (~140–160 chars). Only used for SET_METADATA. Omit to leave unchanged.

featuredImageUrl.description: Featured image URL for social sharing. Only used for SET_METADATA. Omit to leave unchanged.

language.description: ISO-639-1 language code (e.g. "en", "de"). Used for SET_METADATA (omit to leave unchanged).

headHtml.description: Raw HTML injected into <head> (e.g. "<style>body{background:#2563eb}</style>"). Only used for SET_METADATA. Omit to leave unchanged.

revisionId.description: Revision ID to restore. Required for RESTORE_REVISION. Find IDs via action=REVISIONS.

hublSource.description: Complete HubL template source. Required for CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE and UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE. Must be a valid HubL document — real HubL expressions, not escaped HTML. {{ standard_header_includes }} and {{ standard_footer_includes }} are injected automatically before </head> and before </body> if absent. Accepted size: up to 1,500,000 bytes of UTF-8 (1.5 MB).

operationsJson.description: Required for action=BATCH. JSON array of operations to run sequentially, in order. Each element is an object shaped like a single manage_landing_page request: {"action":"...", ...the fields that action needs}. Example: [{"action":"SET_MODULE_FIELDS","contentId":123,"moduleId":"m1","fieldOverridesJson":"{\"heading\":\"Hi\"}"},{"action":"REMOVE","contentId":123,"moduleId":"m2"}]. Only batchable sub-actions are allowed (all READ actions, plus SET_MODULE_FIELDS, SET_MODULE_STYLES, SET_SECTION_STYLES, SET_METADATA, REMOVE, REMOVE_SECTION, MOVE); INSERT, the CREATE/CLONE/UPDATE lifecycle actions, PUBLISH, RESTORE_REVISION, and nested BATCH are rejected before anything runs. The batch STOPS at the first failing operation: operations before it stay committed (there is no rollback), and operations after it are reported as "skipped". The array size must not exceed the server's configured maximum. Each operation's own required fields (contentId, moduleId, etc.) must be present on that element.

businessUnitId.description: ID of the business unit (brand) to put the page in. Used for CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE and CLONE. Omit or pass 0 for the account's default business unit (CLONE then keeps the source page's business unit).

moduleName.description: Display name for a custom module type, as it appears in the editor's module list (e.g. "Pricing Card"). Required for CREATE_MODULE, optional for UPDATE_MODULE. Also seeds the module's Design Manager path, so keep it short and specific.

name: discover_hubspot_schema
description:
Discovers HubSpot data types, pipelines, and stages.

<capabilities>
- Searches across all HubSpot data types available to the current user
- Returns type names that can be used as input to other tools
- Shows read/write access status for each type based on the current user's permissions
- Returns pipelines and their stages (including open/closed status) for a data type
</capabilities>

<usage_guidance>
- Use this tool FIRST when you need to identify which data types exist before querying data
- Use SEARCH_OBJECT_TYPES when you don't know the exact type name
- Use GET_OBJECT_TYPES when you already know the type names (e.g. CONTACT, DEAL), or with an empty typeNameFilter list to retrieve all available types
- Use GET_PIPELINES to list the pipelines and stages for a type (e.g. deal or ticket stages)
- GET_PIPELINES stage metadata: `probability` (DEAL only) is the likelihood (0-1) the deal closes successfully. `state` (all other types) is OPEN or CLOSED, except for LEAD where the values are NEW, IN_PROGRESS, QUALIFIED, or UNQUALIFIED — QUALIFIED and UNQUALIFIED are the closed/terminal states, NEW and IN_PROGRESS are open
- Check readAccess/writeAccess before attempting operations on a type
</usage_guidance>

<examples>
  <example>
    <user_input>How many support requests did we get last month?</user_input>
    <tool_call>{"query": {"_queryType": "SEARCH_OBJECT_TYPES", "searchTerms": "support requests tickets"}}</tool_call>
  </example>

  <example>
    <user_input>How many products do we have?</user_input>
    <thoughts>"products" is ambiguous — it may be HubSpot's standard Products object or a custom object like p12345_product_models, and semantic search tends to rank the standard one first, so I won't just take the top hit. I'll review all candidates and, if more than one plausibly matches, ask the user to clarify before querying.</thoughts>
    <tool_call>{"query": {"_queryType": "SEARCH_OBJECT_TYPES", "searchTerms": "products"}}</tool_call>
  </example>

  <example>
    <user_input>What fields are on contacts and deals?</user_input>
    <tool_call>{"query": {"_queryType": "GET_OBJECT_TYPES", "typeNameFilter": ["CONTACT", "DEAL"]}}</tool_call>
  </example>

  <example>
    <user_input>What types of data does HubSpot have?</user_input>
    <tool_call>{"query": {"_queryType": "GET_OBJECT_TYPES"}}</tool_call>
  </example>

  <example>
    <user_input>What are the deal pipeline stages?</user_input>
    <tool_call>{"query": {"_queryType": "GET_PIPELINES", "objectType": "DEAL"}}</tool_call>
  </example>
</examples>

name: search_conversations
description:
Search or analyze conversation threads, ticket transcripts, and support case messages from HubSpot inboxes. For conversation content tied to a CONTACT, TICKET, DEAL, or COMPANY, including when summarizing or describing a ticket, use this tool, not search_crm_objects/get_crm_objects, which return only record properties, not the message thread. You may use search_crm_objects first to resolve the CRM record ID, then pass it here as objectType + objectId (e.g. objectType=TICKET) to retrieve the thread. Searching NOTE, EMAIL, or CALL engagement objects does not retrieve inbox conversation transcripts. Internal notes and team comments left on a conversation or case live inside the conversation thread, not in NOTE engagements. Retrieve them here with includeAllDialogue=true.

Pick one mode per call, or omit all to get the most recent conversations (newest first), with inbox/channel/status filters still applied. Modes: CRM object (objectType + objectId), time range (startTime/endTime), text search (query, with searchMethod=KEYWORD default or SEMANTIC), or aggregation (aggregationDimensions). Text search with either method may combine with time range; no other cross-mode combinations allowed. Aggregation always counts conversations started in the requested window (hs_started_at). Non-aggregation time-range search counts conversations active in the window (hs_lastmodifieddate) — a conversation started before the window but updated within it will appear in time-range results but not in aggregation counts.

<usage_guidance>
- [Important] For queries like "my conversations" or "our chats" that imply owner/assignee filtering: use the assignedAgentId request filter to narrow to a specific agent's conversations (pass the HubSpot user id, i.e. the <userId> in actor id "A-<userId>"). Each result also includes assignedAgentId for grouping. For wide owner scans, combine with includeMessages=false to scan cheaply
- [Important] Attribute agent/rep names by identity, never from message text (signatures are free text and often wrong). Prefer the resolved names this tool already returns: assignedAgentName for a conversation's assignee and, with messageDetail=FULL, senderName on each agent message. Only when a name is absent, fall back to the id (assignedAgentId, or the <userId> in a sender's "A-<userId>" actorId) and resolve it with search_crm_objects on USER by hs_internal_user_id (or search_owners when owner id == user id) — not get_crm_objects by object id, which is a different id. actorType=AGENT alone does not prove a human sender
- [Important] When a name matches multiple CRM object types (e.g. "Alex Chen" matches both a CONTACT and a COMPANY), you MUST call search_conversations for EACH matching object type — do not stop after the first match. Present results from all matches and tell the user which object types you found
- For channel filters, call get_conversation_channel_metadata first. Use conversationChannelId for a channel type such as EMAIL, and channelInstanceId for a specific configured address, number, or form. To label CHANNEL aggregation buckets, read the channelName already on each bucket instead of calling get_conversation_channel_metadata
- For time-range searches, state the exact dates you used
- For a plain "last N days" or recency search (not aggregation, which requires both time bounds), set startTime only and omit endTime; pinning endTime to the current moment can drop a conversation modified moments earlier
- When choosing between CRM-object lookup and text search, briefly say which you picked and why
- For text search, KEYWORD is the default. Pick the method by whether the request's distinctive terms would plausibly appear VERBATIM in the messages, not by how conversational the request sounds: a loosely-phrased question about a specific thing ("any recent updates on the SAML setup problems?") is still KEYWORD, because "SAML" is what the messages say. Use KEYWORD for product names, error codes, field names, and jargon; use searchMethod=SEMANTIC when there is no such term to match on, for paraphrase, cross-language, or a described situation ("customer frustrated about being locked out"). If SEMANTIC plus one KEYWORD fallback both return nothing relevant, report no matching conversation found (it may just be not recently indexed) rather than re-searching
- [Important] One focused search is almost always enough: if the first search_conversations call returns relevant conversations, summarize them. Do not re-run reworded or synonym queries, and never fire parallel queries for variations of one request. Only broaden to an alternate phrasing when the first returns nothing or clearly misses
- When you already know you need message content, set includeMessages=true on the first call rather than scanning with includeMessages=false and then re-running the same query for messages. Use includeMessages=false only for wide queries where you need to count or filter across many conversations before deciding which ones to read
- Use the minimal messageDetail for the task: the default WITH_ROLE fits most summaries; use TEXT_ONLY when speaker roles are irrelevant; request FULL only when you actually need full per-message metadata, not as a default
- Paginate by passing a response's nextPageAfter back as the after parameter. When a response has no nextPageAfter, you have the last page, so stop; do not invent, increment, or guess a cursor to fetch more
- For partial results, list which objects had conversations and which didn't
- When summarizing, include the number of messages returned; note this may be capped by messageLimit (default 100) and may not reflect the full conversation
- For "how many conversations mention X", use text search and read totalConversations. Name an inbox to get a distinct-conversation count for that inbox/time scope (approximate only for very large match counts); it counts ALL keyword matches and can exceed the page returned. Without an inbox, totalConversations reflects only the returned page, not a portal-wide total. The count reflects the keyword match only, so treat it as approximate whenever conversationChannelId, channelInstanceId, or conversationStatus is set (those filters and blocked-channel exclusions are applied client-side after the count is computed). It can also be positive even when no conversations are returned (matches scored below the relevance floor). Set maxConversations low (and includeMessages=false) for a cheap count
- [Important] For "why are customers contacting us / common reasons / support themes" questions, use conversations, not tickets alone (chat and email may never become a ticket). There is no topic/reason dimension: summarize themes from a small time-range sample (includeMessages=true) and say the result is a sample; aggregation (CHANNEL, STATUS, STARTED_AT_DAY/WEEK) gives volume and trend, not topics
</usage_guidance>

objectType.description: CRM object type: CONTACT, TICKET, DEAL, or COMPANY. Required with objectId for CRM-object mode.

objectId.description: CRM object ID. Required with objectType for CRM-object mode.

Optional: omit to search from the beginning of time up to endTime. May combine with query. With STARTED_AT_* aggregationDimensions, buckets follow the portal's time zone, so for a non-UTC portal a date-only window can return partial first and last buckets.
