includeAllDialogue.description: Include bot/system messages: live-chat initial messages, agent internal notes, workflow messages, bulk SMS, AI agent responses. Default false (human/agent only).

query.description: Search query for text-search mode. Searches message body + email subject. searchMethod selects how it matches: KEYWORD does literal terms and is the default, SEMANTIC matches by meaning. Quote for an exact phrase in KEYWORD mode. Recently-sent messages may not be searchable yet. totalConversations is pre-filter hits and may exceed returned. No pagination. May combine with startTime/endTime to restrict results to that window.

searchMethod.description: Text-query search method. KEYWORD (default): literal term / BM25 match. SEMANTIC: by-meaning, paraphrase, and cross-language match, ordered by relevance; requires query, allows startTime/endTime, rejects after and inboxId.

includeMessages.description: Whether messages are included. Default true (one call returns content inline). Set false to return only metadata (conversationId, threadId, timestamps) for wide count/filter queries; for a normal content request keep the default rather than scanning then re-querying.

messageDetail.description: Per-message shape. TEXT_ONLY, WITH_ROLE, FULL. TEXT_ONLY = messageId+text+createdAt+messageType. WITH_ROLE adds derived actorType (cv-actors ActorType: e.g. AGENT, VISITOR, SYSTEM) and senderContactId. FULL adds full senders/recipients/channel metadata, including each sender's actorId. For an agent sender, actorId (messageSenders[].actorId) is "A-<userId>" (e.g. "A-12345") where userId is the HubSpot user id, not a CRM object/contact id and not a hubspot_owner_id (the CRM owner property value); for a visitor sender it is "V-<contactId>" (e.g. "V-67890") where contactId is the CRM contact id. To attribute an agent by name, prefer the resolved senderName on the message (and assignedAgentName on the conversation); only when that is absent, resolve this actorId's userId to a user record. Never read an agent's name from the message text, which may be a templated or bot signature that does not match the real sender. Default WITH_ROLE. Pass FULL only when the caller needs the full senders/recipients/channel graph; at max page volume FULL responses can exceed MCP-client size caps. Ignored when includeMessages=false or in aggregation mode.

aggregationDimensions.description: Aggregation mode dimensions: STATUS, CHANNEL, STARTED_AT_DAY, STARTED_AT_WEEK. Pass several dimensions in a SINGLE call to get multiple breakdowns at once (e.g. [STATUS, CHANNEL] returns one independent bucket list per dimension, not a crosstab); do not make a separate call per dimension. STARTED_AT_* requires startTime+endTime. STARTED_AT_DAY and STARTED_AT_WEEK are mutually exclusive — at most one date-histogram dimension per call. Empty (default) = non-aggregation mode.

maxBucketsPerDimension.description: Max buckets per dimension. Default 90, max 100. For date histograms, a request is rejected when the number of calendar buckets it spans exceeds min(this, 90) in both UTC and the portal's time zone, so a non-UTC portal can receive one extra partial bucket.

name: get_user_details
description:
Returns user, team and hub info; CRM/marketing object and tool availability.

Call this before other HubSpot operations to establish the current user's identity, permissions, and which object types and tools are available. Returns info for the current user only — to find other users/owners, search the "users" objectType with search_crm_objects.

<usage_guidance>
- Object availability drives which objectType values other tools accept. Each object type has TWO statuses: `read` (view/search) and `write` (create/update) — check the one matching your operation.
- Also reports availability of the other MCP tools; trust this over a tool's own listing, especially when a tool is not AVAILABLE.
- Any non-AVAILABLE object or tool needs user action to resolve (some issues the user alone cannot fix) — surface it only if the task requires that object/tool.
- `include` selects sections: omitted/empty returns USER_INFORMATION + TOOL_INFORMATION; TEAMS_AND_ROLES must be requested explicitly.
- TEAMS_AND_ROLES is personal context only (the user's primary team with member owner IDs, job title, seats, direct report owner IDs). For org-wide teams/roles, "my teams", or account settings (timezone, currency, account type), use get_organization_details.
- directReports are NOT team members. If the user asks about direct reports and directReports is empty, tell them none are configured and ask before substituting team members — never substitute automatically.
</usage_guidance>

Availability statuses:
- AVAILABLE: usable
- REQUIRES_REAUTHORIZATION: disconnect and reconnect the connector
- REQUIRES_PERMISSION_MODIFICATION: user lacks a HubSpot permission
- REQUIRES_ACCOUNT_MODIFICATION: account needs an upgrade
- BLOCKED_FOR_PORTALS_WITH_SENSITIVE_DATA: sensitive data, unresolvable
- NOT_AVAILABLE: no user action can enable it

Returns:
- userId and hubId (accountId)
- `guidance` (if present): relay its message to the user
- `onboarded` (if present): false = portal has not completed initial setup

include.description:
Optional list of data sections to include in the user details response.
Available values:
- USER_INFORMATION: The current user's personal details (owner ID, name, email)
- TOOL_INFORMATION: Tool and CRM object type availability, including separate read/write access per object type
- TEAMS_AND_ROLES: The user's team memberships and role assignments

If not specified or empty, USER_INFORMATION and TOOL_INFORMATION sections are returned.
Specify only the sections you need to reduce response size.
Unrecognized values will result in an error.

name: search_crm_objects
description:
Searches and retrieves CRM records from HubSpot by filters, associations, and criteria. Returns actual records, not field definitions (use search_properties to discover fields, discover_hubspot_schema to discover object types).

Returns: id, requested properties, urlTemplate, total (match count for analytics/pagination), offset.

Rules:
- objectType MUST be an exact type identifier. Standard types (CONTACT, DEAL) work directly; for any concept noun ("lead", "appointment", "account"), ALWAYS call discover_hubspot_schema for its typeName — never infer from training data, as schemas are portal-specific (e.g. "lead" may be a LEAD or a CONTACT lifecycle stage). Re-resolve if results are empty/unexpected.
- To learn a type's data model or recover from 0 results, sample via get_crm_objects (no properties) and confirm values with search_properties before refining filters.
- Max 5 filterGroups, up to 6 filters each, 18 total.
- Always check total; never substitute sample/partial data for actual data.
- Prefer this tool for record retrieval; for complex analysis, refine requirements with the user and segment large datasets.
- You MUST return a clickable URL (from urlTemplate, with UTM params) for every record.
- Use associatedWith to filter/list objects by association; use search_owners to list users/owners.
- First-person queries ("my deals", "contacts I own") MUST filter hubspot_owner_id = {ownerId} from get_user_details; fetching ownerId without applying it returns all records, not the user's.
- Currency: when returning a currency amount (DEAL.amount, LINE_ITEM.price, QUOTE.hs_quote_amount, INVOICE.hs_amount_billed, CART/ORDER.hs_total_price, SUBSCRIPTION.hs_mrr, COMMERCE_PAYMENT.hs_initial_amount) also request its currency-code property (DEAL: deal_currency_code; LINE_ITEM: hs_line_item_currency_code; QUOTE/INVOICE: hs_currency; else hs_currency_code). For DEAL aggregation use amount_in_home_currency (never pair with deal_currency_code); never sum raw amount across differing currencies.

objectType.description:
Mandatory field specifying the ObjectType to search for objects for.

Well-known standard CRM types (e.g. CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL, TICKET, and other documented HubSpot objects) can be used directly. Any other type is a custom object identified by a portal-prefixed ID of the form `p<portalId>_<name>` (e.g. `p885186001_fleet_vehicles`) that you MUST obtain from `discover_hubspot_schema` before searching — do not construct or guess it.
A plausible standard-looking name (e.g. `products`) may actually resolve to a different standard object OR a custom object. When you are not certain a name is a standard type, treat it as non-standard and resolve it via `discover_hubspot_schema` first, then use the exact `typeName` it returns.

query.description:
Optional text to search for within the default searchable properties of the specified object type.
Uses simple text matching (contains)
Each object type has different searchable properties.
contacts - firstname, lastname, email, phone, company),
companies - name, website, domain, phone),
deals - dealname, pipeline, dealstage, description, dealtype)
ticket - subject, content, hs_pipeline_stage, hs_ticket_category, hs_ticket_id)

[Important] Common stop words (e.g., "the", "a", "of", "and", "in") may not be indexed for some object types. If a query returns no results, retry by removing stop words or using property filters instead of free-text search.

Max length - 200 chars

properties.description: Optional list of property names to include in results. Returns default set if empty. Specify the minimum set of properties needed for the task for best results. Leave it empty only if you explicitly need to discover the full default property set.

propertyName.description: The name of the property to sort by

sorts.description: Optional sorting rules for results. Only one sort rule can be applied

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page. Max: 200, Default: 100

propertyName.description:
Specify the name of the Crm Object Property to filter on.

DO NOT use the pseudo-property `associations.{objectType}` or `associated_{objectType}` for associations.

You can use the following properties to filter by the number of associated records:

Tickets - hs_num_associated_companies
Companies - num_associated_contacts, num_associated_deals
Contacts - num_associated_deals
Deals - num_associated_contacts

operator.description:
Filter operator:
  EQ, NEQ, LT, LTE, GT, GTE, BETWEEN, IN, NOT_IN, HAS_PROPERTY, NOT_HAS_PROPERTY, CONTAINS_TOKEN, NOT_CONTAINS_TOKEN
Usage:
  No additional parameters required for HAS_PROPERTY and NOT_HAS_PROPERTY

value.description: Value parameter for single-value operators (EQ, NEQ, LT, LTE, GT, GTE, CONTAINS_TOKEN, NOT_CONTAINS_TOKEN)

highValue.description: High value for range-based operators like BETWEEN

values.description: Set of values for multi-value operators like IN and NOT_IN

items.description:
Represents a filter condition for CRM object searches.
 Filters specify criteria that property values must meet to be included in search results.
 The available operators are defined in {@link PropertyFilterOperator}.

filters.description: Set of filters in this group. All filters combined with logical ANDThe filter is used with associatedWith for AND logic in the same FilterGroup.

objectType.description:
Object type to find associations with.

Example: "companies" to find records associated with a company

operator.description:
Operator for association filtering:
- EQUAL/NOT_EQUAL: Associated with the specified object.
- IN/NOT_IN: Associated with any of the specified objects.

objectIds.description:
DEPRECATED: Use objectIdValues instead.
List of object IDs as strings to filter by.
If both objectIds and objectIdValues are provided, objectIdValues takes precedence.
Valid IDs are string representations of positive longs (e.g., '123', '456').

For EQUAL and NOT_EQUAL operators, provide exactly one ID eg. ["123"]
For IN and NOT_IN operators, provide multiple IDs eg. ["123", "456", "789"]

objectIdValues.description:
List of object IDs to filter by.

At least one valid object ID must be provided.
Each object ID greater than 0.
Maximum of 100 object IDs allowed per association filter.

For EQUAL and NOT_EQUAL operators, provide exactly one ID eg. [123]
For IN and NOT_IN operators, provide multiple IDs eg. [123, 456, 789]

associatedWith.description:
Association filters for finding records related to specific objects (e.g., "contacts for company X").

Within a single FilterGroup, all association filters are combined with AND logic.
Association filters are also ANDed with any property filters in the same FilterGroup.

Examples:
- Find contacts associated with company 123:
  [{"objectType": "companies", "operator": "EQUAL", "objectIdValues": [123]}]

- Find contacts associated with company 123 OR 456 (use IN operator):
  [{"objectType": "companies", "operator": "IN", "objectIdValues": [123, 456]}]

- Find records associated with BOTH company 123 AND contact 456 (multiple filters):
  [{"objectType": "companies", "operator": "EQUAL", "objectIdValues": [123]},
   {"objectType": "contacts", "operator": "EQUAL", "objectIdValues": [456]}]

- To search for company A OR company B, use separate FilterGroups (FilterGroups are ORed together).

items.description:
Represents a group of filters that are logically connected with AND operators.
 Multiple filter groups in a search request are combined with OR operators.

filterGroups.description:
* The filter groups that define the search criteria.
 * Filters that match ALL of several conditions (AND logic) should be put in the same filterGroup.
 * Filters that match AT LEAST ONE of several conditions (OR logic) should be put in a separate filterGroup.

userIntent.description:
The original intent or goal the user was trying to accomplish.
Set to "<unchanged>" if the intent has already been submitted and hasn't changed.
Use generic or anonymized references instead of specific names, emails, or other PII.
Replace specific names with generalized references:
- Company/Partner names: "Bluleadz partner" → "partner A"
- Deal names: "Tesla deal" → "deal A"
- Customer names: "Acme Corp customer" → "company X"
Important: Avoid adding extraneous information other than what the user provides in the current chat.
Maximum 40 words.

satisfaction.description:
The user's satisfaction during the conversation.
  Set to DISSATISFIED when the user struggled with a feature, mentioned an unmet need or showed dissatisfaction.
  <dissatisfied_signals>
  - User provides explicit correction: "No, I meant...", "Actually, I want..."
  - User repeats query with different phrasing
  - User states something is wrong: "That's wrong", "That's not right"
  - User clarifies because agent misunderstood
  </dissatisfied_signals>
  Set to SATISFIED when the user expresses satisfaction, gratitude, or approval.
  Set to NEUTRAL when the conversation flowed smoothly without strong emotional signals.

chatInsights.description:
Insights about the chat including user intent and satisfaction level.
IMPORTANT: MUST be provided for all scenarios.

name: manage_crm_objects
description:
Creates or updates CRM objects and their associations. Use createRequest to create objects; use updateRequest to update existing objects or associate two existing objects. For any association or association-label work, first call the `tool_guidance` tool for `manage_crm_objects` — detailed association steps live there.

<required_first_step>
BEFORE proposing or making any change, call get_user_details and check write availability for the target objectType. If write is not AVAILABLE (e.g. REQUIRES_PERMISSION_MODIFICATION), do NOT show a confirmation table and do NOT call this tool — explain the limitation to the user and stop.
</required_first_step>

<mandatory_confirmation>
Before every create or update, show the proposed changes in a table (columns: Object Type | ID | Property | Current Value | New Value) and get explicit user approval. This is CRITICAL.
- Use human-friendly property labels ("Deal Stage", not "dealstage") and enum display labels ("Closed Won", not "closedwon"); if you lack label info from a prior call, fetch it with search_properties first.
- End with an approval prompt, e.g. "Approve? [✅ Yes / ❌ No]".
- On the FIRST confirmation only, also add: "Want to skip confirmations for this chat? Just ask." Then stop offering it but keep confirming. If the user opts out, skip confirmations for the session.
</mandatory_confirmation>

<guidance>
- Limit to a MAXIMUM of 10 objects per request (upserts and associations).
- Not all properties are editable. Use search_properties to list properties, or search_crm_objects to sample data, before changes.
- hubspot_owner_id defaults to the current user when omitted; set it to empty string to leave unowned.
- For concept nouns ("lead", "appointment", "account"), ALWAYS call discover_hubspot_schema first for the exact typeName — never infer from training data; schemas are portal-specific (e.g. "lead" may be LEAD or a CONTACT lifecycle stage), and creating the wrong object type cannot be undone.
</guidance>

objectType.description: The object type to create (e.g., contacts, companies, deals, tickets)

properties.description: The property keys and associated values for each key to set on the newly created object

associations.description:
Optional list of associations to create with this object.
For CREATE operations, associations are created after the object is successfully created.
Each association requires a target object ID & target object type.

objects.description: A list of CRM objects to create

createRequest.description: Required when creating new CRM objects.

objectType.description: The object type to update (e.g., contacts, companies, deals, tickets)

objectId.description: The ID of the object to update

properties.description: The property keys and values to update on the existing object. Leave empty to only create associations

associations.description:
Optional list of associations to create with this object.
For UPDATE operations, associations are created after the object is successfully updated.
Each association requires a target object ID and target object type.

objects.description: A list of CRM objects to update

updateRequest.description: Required when updating existing CRM objects.

confirmationStatus.description: Indicates whether the user has approved this action. Must be CONFIRMED or CONFIRMATION_WAIVED_FOR_SESSION before invoking the tool.

targetObjectId.description: The ID of the target object to associate with

targetObjectType.description: The object type of the target object (e.g., CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL)

labels.description:
List of association label names to add to this association.
Labels must already exist for the object type pair (e.g., "Contact with Primary Company", "Billing Contact").
Specified labels are added to any existing labels on the association.
If not specified, only the default association is created/updated and existing labels are left unchanged.

name: get_marketing_email_analytics
description:
Provides analytics data for marketing emails based on sends in the given date range. To find emails created or published within certain date ranges, use search_crm_objects instead.

The request takes a single field, analysisRequest, which is an OBJECT — never a bare string. It carries a "_type" discriminator plus the section settings for that type. 
Available analysisRequest types (set as analysisRequest._type):
- "OVERVIEW" — portal-level aggregate statistics (sends, deliveries, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes)   over a date range, optionally scoped to specific emails or broken down by time interval.   Uses statisticsSection.
- "HEALTH" — portal email health diagnostics. Four sections:   mxGroupStatisticsSection (delivery performance statistics by the destination domains with the most deliveries, over a date range);   healthScoresSection (monthly 0–100 health scores with per-metric breakdown for   click, open, hard bounce, spam report, unsubscribe, and click-to-open — up to 6 months,   GLOBAL or INDUSTRY benchmark);   sourceHealthScoresSection (same per-metric breakdown per contact source, i.e.   where contacts were imported from, past ~30 days);   bounceReasonsSection (breakdown of bounces by reason category over a date range,   split into hard and soft bounces, optionally scoped to a single MX group).
- "RECIPIENTS" — delivery outcome and engagement summary for a specific contact recipient,   with an optional ordered event timeline (sent, opened, clicked, bounced, etc.).   Uses recipientDetailsSection.   No operation returns a collection of all recipients for an email;   only individual recipient information is available.
- "UNSUBSCRIBE_SURVEY" — breakdown of unsubscribe survey responses by reason code   (NO_LONGER_INTERESTED, DID_NOT_SIGN_UP, TOO_MANY_EMAILS, IRRELEVANT_CONTENT, OTHER)   over a date range. Optionally scoped to a specific email by emailContentId.   Use this to understand WHY contacts unsubscribed and improve future emails.

analysisRequest.description: The analysis request object. Set '_type' to 'OVERVIEW', 'HEALTH', or 'RECIPIENTS' and include the corresponding section settings.

mode.description: Deprecated alias for analysisRequest; use analysisRequest instead.

_type.description: Email health diagnostics. Supports portal-level health scores, deliverability stats per MX group, and health scores per contact source.

startDate.description: Required. Start of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd. The date range must not exceed six months.

endDate.description: Required. End of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd. The date range must not exceed six months.

frequency.description: Aggregation for the results. Use TOTAL to return a single aggregated value for the full date range. Use DAILY, WEEKLY, or MONTHLY to return a time series broken down by that interval. Defaults to MONTHLY.

limit.description: Maximum number of top MX groups to return when no MX group filter is provided. Defaults to 10.

mxGroups.description: MX groups to filter by (e.g. "gmail.com", "outlook.com"). If empty, the top N groups by delivered volume are used.

emailType.description: Restrict results to emails of this type. Omit to include all email types.

marketingEmailObjectIds.description: Restrict results to these marketing email object IDs (hs_object_id on the MARKETING_EMAIL CRM object, returned as a String by CRM search tools — cast to Long before passing here).

filters.description: Filters to restrict which data is included in the results.

mxGroupStatisticsSection.description: MX group statistics section. Provide to query performance statistics broken down by the destination domains with the most deliveries.

scoreType.description: Whether to evaluate scores against global absolute thresholds (GLOBAL) or against industry benchmarks (INDUSTRY). Defaults to GLOBAL.

numberOfMonths.description: Number of months of history to return, counting back from the current month (inclusive). Must be between 1 and 6. Defaults to 6.

healthScoresSection.description: Health scores section. Provide to query monthly portal health scores for a configurable number of months, including per-metric breakdown.

sourceHealthScoresSection.description: Source health scores section. Provide to query health scores broken down by contact source (where contacts were imported from). Covers the service-configured window, currently 30 days.

startDate.description: Required. Start of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd. The date range must not exceed six months.

endDate.description: Required. End of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd. The date range must not exceed six months.

mxGroup.description: Restrict the breakdown to a single MX group (e.g. "gmail.com", "outlook.com"). Omit to include bounces across all MX groups.

bounceReasonsSection.description: Bounce reasons section. Provide to query a breakdown of bounces by reason category, split into hard and soft bounces, for the portal.

_type.description: Recipient-level data for a specific contact that received a marketing email.

marketingEmailObjectId.description: Required. The marketing email object ID — the hs_object_id property on the MARKETING_EMAIL CRM object, returned as a String by CRM search tools. Cast to Long before passing here.

contactCrmObjectId.description: Required. The CONTACT CRM object ID of the recipient to look up.

includeEvents.description: When true, fetches the full ordered event timeline for this recipient (sent, opened, clicked, bounced, etc.). Defaults to false to avoid the extra round-trip when only the delivery summary is needed.

recipientDetailsSection.description: Recipient details section: delivery outcome, engagement summary, and optional event timeline for a specific contact.

_type.description: Breakdown of unsubscribe survey responses by reason code over a date range.

startDate.description: Required. Start of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

endDate.description: Required. End of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

emailContentId.description: Optional. Marketing email content ID (hs_object_id on MARKETING_EMAIL, cast from String to Long). When provided, returns survey responses scoped to sends of this specific email. When omitted, returns portal-wide aggregate data.

includeOtherTexts.description: When true, the response includes the raw free-text entries submitted by contacts who selected 'Other' as their reason. Use this when you intend to summarize or analyze the verbatim feedback. Defaults to false.

_type.description: Portal-level aggregate send statistics broken down over a date range.

startDate.description: Required. Start of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd. The date range must not exceed one calendar year.

endDate.description: Required. End of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd. The date range must not exceed one calendar year.

frequency.description: Aggregation for the results. Use TOTAL to return a single aggregated value for the full date range. Use DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, or YEARLY to return a time series broken down by that interval. Defaults to MONTHLY.

marketingEmailObjectIds.description: Restrict results to these marketing email object IDs (hs_object_id on the MARKETING_EMAIL CRM object, returned as a String by CRM search tools — cast to Long before passing here).

filters.description: Filters to restrict which data is included in the results.

dimensions.description: Dimensions to group results by. Each data point will include a value for each requested dimension. Use MARKETING_EMAIL_ID to split results per marketing email.

statisticsSection.description: Statistics section. Provide to request portal-level send statistics broken down over a date range and time interval.

name: search_owners
description:
Lists and searches for owners who can be assigned to CRM records.

<capabilities>
- Supports searching by name/email or batch lookup by owner IDs
- HubSpot owner ids and user IDs are distinct, lookups only work when owner ids are provided specifically
</capabilities>

<returns>
List of owner objects containing:
- ownerId: The ID to use for hubspot_owner_id assignments
- name: Display name of the owner
- isActive: Whether the owner is currently active
</returns>

<examples>
  <example>
    <description>Search by name</description>
    <query>{"searchQuery": "John Smith"}</query>
  </example>

  <example>
    <description>Lookup specific IDs</description>
    <query>{"ownerIds": [12345, 67890]}</query>
  </example>

  <example>
    <description>Paginate results</description>
    <query>{"limit": 50, "offset": 50}</query>
  </example>
</examples>

searchQuery.description: Optional search query to find owners by name or email. Returns all owners if not provided

ownerIds.description: Optional list of owner IDs to lookup directly. When provided, search query is ignored

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 25, max 100

name: manage_marketing_email
description:
Manages a marketing email's settings and content. Call tool_guidance for guidance.

Settings sub-operations (_type):
- "LIST_SUBSCRIPTION_TYPES" — list subscription types;   call before CREATE to get a valid subscriptionTypeId
- "LIST_FROM_ADDRESSES" — list verified from addresses;   call before CREATE to choose a replyToEmail;   if address not listed, list options and stop
- "CREATE" — create a new email   (required: name, subject, fromName, replyToEmail, subscriptionTypeId;   permanent fields — ask the user BEFORE calling CREATE:   templatePath: ask template or blank? call LIST_TEMPLATES to show options;   brandId; emailType: BATCH by default, AUTOMATED for workflow emails)
- "POLL_EMAIL_CREATION" — poll for CRM object; takes marketingEmailId
- "UPDATE" — update email settings;   template/brandId cannot be changed after creation
- "CLONE" — clone into a new draft
- "GET_EMAIL_DETAILS" — retrieve current settings
- "GET_TEMPLATE" — retrieve a template by path
- "LIST_TEMPLATES" — search/browse templates by kind   (CODED or DND) and filename

Content sub-operations (marketingEmailObjectId):
- "GET_CONTENT" — returns the editable layout
- "EDIT_CONTENT" — always call tool_guidance; resubmit   full layout; preserve all styling, only change text/links/images
- "PREVIEW_CONTENT" — renders the email; returns   subjectLine, renderedText, (optional) renderedHtml
- "AB_TEST_EMAIL" — set up an A/B test on a draft email by adding Version B;   use this whenever the user asks to test two versions, create a version B, split test,   or try two subject lines — they often don't say "A/B" explicitly

Only draft emails can be edited. Always show proposed changes and get explicit user confirmation before creating, updating, or editing.

name.description: Required. Internal name for the email (e.g., 'Spring Sale 2026').

fromName.description: Required. The sender's display name (e.g., 'Marketing Team').

subscriptionTypeId.description: Required. The subscription type ID. Determines which contacts are eligible.

brandId.description: The brand ID (also called business unit ID). Required for portals with multiple brands. Cannot be changed after creation — ask the user before creating.

includeListIds.description: Contact list IDs to include as recipients. Required before scheduling.

exclusionListIds.description: Contact list IDs to exclude (suppression lists).

includeContactIds.description: Individual contact VIDs to include as recipients. Use instead of or alongside includeListIds.

campaignCrmObjectId.description: The CRM object ID of the CAMPAIGN to associate with this email.

templatePath.description: Template path from LIST_TEMPLATES. Omit for a blank email. Cannot be changed after creation.

previewText.description: Preview text shown in email clients before the message is opened (typically 50–100 chars).

emailType.description: The type of email to create. BATCH (default) for marketing blasts sent to contact lists at a scheduled time. AUTOMATED for workflow-triggered emails — recipients are enrolled via workflows, not contact lists. Cannot be changed via these tools after creation — if a change is needed, the user must update it in the HubSpot UI before publishing.

marketingEmailObjectId.description: The marketing email object ID (hs_object_id on the MARKETING_EMAIL CRM object). Required.

subscriptionTypeId.description: The subscription type ID. Determines which contacts are eligible.

includeListIds.description: Contact list IDs to include as recipients.

exclusionListIds.description: Contact list IDs to exclude (suppression lists).

includeContactIds.description: Individual contact VIDs to include as recipients. Use instead of or alongside includeListIds.

campaignCrmObjectId.description: The CRM object ID of the CAMPAIGN to associate with this email.

previewText.description: Preview text shown in email clients before the message is opened (typically 50–100 chars).

name: query_crm_data
description:
Queries HubSpot CRM data via SQL with HubSpot-specific extensions.
IMPORTANT: You MUST call the Tool Guidance tool before your first query. It contains required guidance and examples.

<select>
IMPORTANT: Property names must exactly match HubSpot internal names. Always call search_properties to confirm names before querying.
The record identifier property is hs_object_id.
For financial values, prefer properties ending in _in_home_currency.
  <unsupported>SELECT DISTINCT, AS aliases, CASE WHEN, IF(), string functions (CONCAT, UPPER, etc.), COALESCE, associations.OBJECT.</unsupported>
</select>

<from>
One object type per query: CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL, TICKET, etc. Use a user-details tool to discover supported types.
  <unsupported>JOIN, UNION, subqueries, CTEs.</unsupported>
</from>

<where>
Operators — comparison: =, !=, <, >, <=, >=; text/substring match: column LIKE '%value%'; presence: column IS NULL / column IS NOT NULL.
List membership: hs_crm_search.ilsListIds = 'LIST_ID' (cannot combine with aggregates or GROUP BY).
Date filters: in an aggregation (GROUP BY or aggregate) use a YYYY-MM-DD date, matched by day; in a plain row SELECT either a date or a full timestamp (e.g. '2025-01-01 14:00:00') works.
"My"/"I" queries: filter by hubspot_owner_id (see Tool Guidance for resolution steps).
</where>

<group-by>
DATE_TRUNC(prop, 'INTERVAL') — INTERVAL: DAY | WEEK | MONTH | QUARTER | YEAR.
MEDIAN(prop) supported alongside standard aggregates.
  <unsupported>HAVING.</unsupported>
</group-by>

<order-by>
Sort direction: ORDER BY column ASC for ascending, DESC for descending.
</order-by>

<cross-object>
To retrieve associated object data, use OBJECT.property (e.g., SELECT COMPANY.name FROM CONTACT) — NOT associations.OBJECT.
associations.OBJECT is for WHERE existence checks only (IS NULL / IS NOT NULL). Never use it in SELECT or GROUP BY.
A query can reference at most 2 different associated object types.
</cross-object>

name: manage_aeo_prompts
description:
Read AI responses to tracked prompts, or create and run new tracked prompts.
Provide exactly one `operation`, a JSON object (not a string) with an
`_operationType` field set to DETAIL (a single prompt's per-run AI response
text, citations, and mentions for an assistant and date window) or CREATE
(start tracking new prompts and run them immediately). CREATE requires a
confirmed=false preview before confirmed=true. Call get_aeo_metrics with
include=["BUSINESS_UNITS"] then include=["ICPS_AND_PRODUCTS"] to get the
businessUnitId, icpIds, and productIds that CREATE needs. Call tool_guidance
(mcpToolInstructions) for the confirmation workflow and per-operation details.

promptId.description: Prompt record ID to drill into. Discover it from get_aeo_metrics include=["PROMPTS"].

startDate.description: ISO-8601 start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; defaults to 30 days ago. Per-run results on or after this date are returned.

endDate.description: ISO-8601 end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; defaults to today. Must be on or after startDate.

aiAssistant.description: AI assistant family to filter runs by (CHATGPT, GEMINI, CLAUDE, PERPLEXITY). Omit to return runs for all assistants.

maxRuns.description: Maximum number of runs to include. Defaults to 10; capped at 25 to stay within the MCP response budget.

businessUnitId.description: Business unit ID. Call get_aeo_metrics with include=["BUSINESS_UNITS"] to discover available business units and their IDs. The business unit must already have an input profile.

promptTexts.description: Optional, for the MANUAL path only: exact prompt texts the user dictated, e.g. "What is the best CRM for small businesses?". Leave EMPTY to have AEO generate the prompts from the icpIds, productIds, and buyingJourneyPhases below (the recommended path) — do not write prompts yourself. In the generated flow the first confirmed=false call starts generation and returns a previewToken; call confirmed=false again with that previewToken until the generated prompts come back, then confirm by passing the previewToken on a confirmed=true call (not the texts).

previewToken.description: The token returned when a confirmed=false call starts AEO generation. Pass it back on subsequent confirmed=false calls to poll for the generated prompts, then on the confirmed=true call (leaving promptTexts empty) to persist the exact prompts AEO generated, each bound to its own ICP, product, and buying-journey phase. Not used for the manual promptTexts path.

buyingJourneyPhases.description: Optional buying-journey phases to generate prompts for (AWARENESS, CONSIDERATION, EVALUATION, DECISION). Used only when promptTexts is empty. Defaults to CONSIDERATION.

numberOfPrompts.description: Optional number of prompts to generate per ICP x product x phase combination (minimum 1). Used only when promptTexts is empty. Defaults to 1.

icpIds.description: ICP IDs to associate with the new prompts. Required. Call get_aeo_metrics with include=["ICPS_AND_PRODUCTS"] to discover valid IDs.

productIds.description: Product IDs to associate with the new prompts. Required. Call get_aeo_metrics with include=["ICPS_AND_PRODUCTS"] to discover valid IDs.

topicIds.description: Optional topic IDs to associate with the new prompts.

confirmed.description: Set to true only after showing the user the preview response and receiving explicit approval. First call must use confirmed=false to get a preview.

operation.description: The prompt operation to perform, as a JSON object (not a string). The object must include an "_operationType" field set to exactly one of "DETAIL" or "CREATE", alongside that operation's own fields. Use DETAIL to drill into a single tracked prompt's run history, or CREATE to create and run new tracked prompts. Provide exactly one operation. Example: {"_operationType": "CREATE", "businessUnitId": 123, "promptTexts": ["What is the best CRM for small businesses?"], "icpIds": [1], "productIds": [2]}.

name: read_campaign_data
description: REQUIRED FIRST STEP: before your first call, invoke tool_guidance for "read_campaign_data" and follow it; it contains the required parameter details and examples for each operation. Reads campaign data using one of four operations selected by the `operation` field. GET_ANALYTICS: engagement metrics (sessions, new contacts, influenced contacts) for one or more campaigns. GET_ASSET_METRICS: performance metrics for assets of one type associated with a campaign. Metrics are type-specific and NOT comparable across types — do NOT use this for cross-type "top/best performing asset" questions; use getCampaignAttributionReports with dimension=ASSET_TITLE for that (its attribution metrics share a common unit across all asset types; set sortByMetric to the metric the question asks about — REVENUE when no metric is specified). GET_CONTACTS: paginated contact IDs attributed to a campaign, filtered by attribution type (NEW_CONTACTS_FIRST_TOUCH, NEW_CONTACTS_LAST_TOUCH, INFLUENCED_CONTACTS). GET_CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES: returns the portal-enabled campaign asset types with human-readable aliases (e.g. AUTOMATION_PLATFORM_FLOW → workflows). No additional request parameters needed.

operation.description: Required. The operation to perform: GET_ANALYTICS, GET_ASSET_METRICS, GET_CONTACTS, or GET_CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES.

campaignCrmObjectId.description: Required. The campaign's numeric CRM object ID (hs_object_id), greater than 0. If you only have the campaign name, look it up first via CRM search or read_campaign_data; do not guess it.

requestedData.description: Required. The type of analytics data to retrieve. Only METRICS is supported — use it for engagement data (sessions, new contacts, influenced contacts). For revenue or attribution data, use getCampaignAttributionReports instead.

startDate.description: Optional start of the date range in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be provided together with endDate or both omitted. If omitted, defaults to the campaign's configured start date or up to 3 years ago.

endDate.description: Optional end of the date range in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be provided together with startDate or both omitted. If omitted, defaults to the campaign's configured end date or today.

name: get_organization_details
description:
Get organization-wide teams, job titles (roles), seats, and account info (timezone, currency, account type, portal name). Use the include parameter (TEAMS, SEATS, JOB_TITLES, ACCOUNT_INFORMATION) to fetch only what you need.

Returns only the included sections (or all if include is omitted):
- TEAMS: teams with name and member owner IDs (org-wide, not personal).
- SEATS: available seat type NAMES only, not user counts.
- JOB_TITLES: roles/job titles present in the org.
- ACCOUNT_INFORMATION: timezone, currency, account type, UI domain, account ID, portal name, create date.
- guidance (optional): if present, read it carefully; it may hold a user-facing message (e.g. missing permissions to relay) or an internal hint (e.g. name disambiguation).

Routing:
- First-person personal context ("my team", "my role", "my manager", "my direct reports") -> use get_user_details instead.
- EXCEPTION: plural "my teams" / "which teams am I on" -> use THIS tool (get_user_details returns only one primaryTeam).
- Org-wide references ("our sales team", "the marketing team", "all managers") -> use this tool.

Follow-ups (this tool alone does not count or list users/deals):
- Count users by seat or role: get seat type names / job titles here, then filter search_crm_objects on the USER objectType by each. SEATS gives names only, so you MUST follow up with search_crm_objects for per-seat counts.
- A team's data ("our sales team's deals"): include=[TEAMS] to resolve members to owner IDs, then pass those IDs as filters to search_crm_objects.
- Which teams a user is on: include=[TEAMS], then match the user's ownerId against team member ownerIds; match on ownerId ONLY, never on member name.

include.description:
Optional list of data to include in the response.
Available values:
- TEAMS: Include the list of teams and their members
- SEATS: Include the list of seat/role names available in the account
- JOB_TITLES: Include the list of job titles assigned to users in the account
- ACCOUNT_INFORMATION: Include account details such as timezone, currency, and account type

If not specified or empty, all data will be returned.
Specify only the values you need to reduce response size.
Unrecognized values will result in an error.

name: manage_onboarding
description: <purpose>Assess a portal's CRM onboarding status and guide the user through the next onboarding step.</purpose><usage_guidance>Call this tool when get_user_details returns onboarded: false — this indicates the portal may be new and not yet set up. After answering the user's immediate question, invoke this tool proactively and offer to help them get started. Do not call this tool if get_user_details returned onboarded: true. Use action to control behavior: leave empty (the default) to just check status. SET_GOAL — records the user's primary goal; requires goal to be set to one of organizeAndTrackContacts, automateMarketing, generateLeads, manageSalesPipeline, customerSupport, billsAndCollectPayment, buildWebsite, createMarketingContent, or stillExploring — map the user's own words to the closest matching value. Only one goal can be stored; setting a new goal replaces any previous one.</usage_guidance><returns>goalStatus: NOT_STARTED or COMPLETE — whether the user has set an onboarding goal; goal: the user's stored goal (present once set); taskGroup: the onboarding task group for that goal (present once the goal is set, unless every task is already done) — a nested structure of a group with a name, a list of childGroups (each with its own name and further childGroups), and tasks, where each task has a name, description, and link the user can open; tasks the user has already completed or skipped are excluded, and taskGroup is omitted entirely when nothing is left to do; guidance: actionable guidance for you, the agent — when present, follow it and present the returned tasks as a set of options for the user to choose from; do not collapse them into a single step</returns><response_rendering>Render every returned task, including those nested in child groups, as a markdown link [task name](task link) with its description. List all of them (guidance says how many); do not omit or limit. Always render: See all onboarding tasks in your [start guide](guideLink).</response_rendering>

action.description: Defaults to empty, which just checks onboarding status. Set to SET_GOAL to record the user's primary goal — requires goal to also be set.

goal.description: The user's primary goal, required when action=SET_GOAL. Map the user's free-text goal description to the single closest matching canonical value: organizeAndTrackContacts, automateMarketing, generateLeads, manageSalesPipeline, customerSupport, billsAndCollectPayment, buildWebsite, createMarketingContent, or stillExploring.

name: search_properties
description:
Finds the most relevant CRM property definitions using keyword-based search.

<capabilities>
- Lists all property definitions for an object type when no search terms are provided
- To search for actual record data, use search_crm_objects
</capabilities>

<returns>
A filtered list of matching properties, each with:
- name: Property identifier
- label: Display label
- description: Property description
- matchScore: Relevance score for the query (absent when no query is provided)
</returns>

<usage_guidance>
- Prefer the keywords field to pass multiple property-name guesses in a SINGLE request (best performance); use the query field for a single guess (backward compatibility)
- Keywords must be property-name guesses (e.g. "assignee", "zip_code"), NOT natural-language phrases
- MAXIMUM 5 keywords per request; exceeding this returns a validation error
- Omit search terms to return ALL properties for the object type (useful for discovery)
</usage_guidance>

<examples>
- "open tickets grouped by urgency" -> {"objectType": "TICKET", "keywords": ["urgency"]}
- "calls assigned to me" -> {"objectType": "CALL", "keywords": ["assignee", "assigned_to", "call_owner", "owned_by"]}
- "companies by name, employee count, zip, last contact" -> {"objectType": "COMPANY", "keywords": ["name", "employees", "zip_code", "last_contact"]}
- "analyze all tickets (property discovery)" -> {"objectType": "TICKET"}
</examples>

objectType.description: The name of the object type to search properties for

query.description:
DEPRECATED: Use keywords instead.
Single search keyword for backward compatibility.
If both query and keywords are provided, keywords takes precedence.
If empty and no keywords provided, returns all properties for the object type.

keywords.description:
Multiple search keywords (max 5) to find relevant properties using efficient keyword-based search.
Supports searching for multiple related property concepts in a single request.

Examples:
- ["urgency"] - Single keyword search
- ["assignee", "assigned_to", "owner"] - Multiple related keywords for assignment
- ["name", "employees", "zip", "contact"] - Multiple unrelated keywords for different properties

If both query and keywords are provided, keywords takes precedence.
If empty and no query provided, returns all properties for the object type.
